rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice in spoken Hong Kong Cantonese.

example.english: Tomorrow is a holiday, so let's go hiking.
example.traditional: 聽日放假，我哋去行山啦。
example.jyutping: ting1 jat6 fong3 gaa3 ngo5 dei6 heoi3 haang4 saan1 laa1

rows.note: Use this less colloquial alternative, especially in Mandarin-influenced or more neutral speech.

example.english: The meeting has been moved to three tomorrow afternoon.
example.traditional: 明天個會改咗下晝三點。
example.jyutping: ming4 tin1 go3 wui2 goi2 zo2 haa6 zau3 saam1 dim2

rows.note: Use this formal or written alternative rather than the everyday spoken choice.

example.english: The exhibition will officially open tomorrow.
example.traditional: 展覽將於明日正式開幕。
example.jyutping: zin2 laam5 zoeng1 jyu1 ming4 jat6 zing3 sik1 hoi1 mok6

rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial Cantonese word for the day after today.

example.english: We’re going for dim sum tomorrow.
example.jyutping: ting1 jat6 ngo5 dei6 heoi3 jam2 caa4

rows.note: Use this as a less distinctly Cantonese alternative to the everyday 聽日.

example.english: The meeting starts at nine tomorrow morning.
example.jyutping: ming4 tin1 ziu1 zou2 gau2 dim2 hoi1 wui2

rows.note: Use this mainly in formal or written contexts for the day after today.

example.english: The results will be announced tomorrow.
example.jyutping: ming4 jat6 zoeng1 gung1 bou3 git3 gwo2
